assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:ernst-zimmerman@original-light-novels#86-ernst-zimmermann-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-5 Ernst Zimmerman character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels, in which he is attested from V02 to V14, with Alter.1 as audited supplemental evidence and Alter.2 excluded. Row counts come only from the profile's own diagnostic scene bank (232 rows, ERN-001 to ERN-232), every row routed to volume, XHTML file and paragraph; the bank does not mark which rows carry a Phase-5 locator, so no Phase-5 or LOCATOR_GAP split is claimed. The shared CMR locator index, the CMR-9 promotion audit and ledger, the profile's validation report, the relationship register matrix, other characters' profiles, the ledgers L01, L02, L03, L08 and L09, Documents 06 and 09, the T09 and T10 tracks, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its HIGH, MODERATE-to-HIGH and OPEN labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume, Alter.2 scene or other character's profile is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The profile's located states from V02 through the V14 boundary. V02 is split at the rescue and citizenship scenes (p-005 ¶283-414), the household and the self-audit with Teresa, the household partner (p-005 ¶443-500), the future-scripting and reenlistment conflict (p-006 ¶345-424) and the correction by Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) with the officer-school condition (p-006 ¶426-507). V03 runs from procedural scrutiny (p-006 ¶59-92) through the command switch and the order to return (p-007 ¶66-138) and the 'die with my ideal' rhetoric (p-008 ¶147-161) to external safeguards for Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (p-014 ¶26-31). V08 is the anti-sacrifice planning and the correction by Shin (p-002 ¶47-74). V12 is institutional self-erasure (p-004 ¶587-602) and private nihilism (p-008 ¶321-333). dimensions.note: The profile gives a causal account of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman): a warm, theatrically casual, institutionally serious guardian whose strength and danger share one root, treating human dignity as an absolute demand without reliably including himself in the humanity it protects. It names three decision trajectories of one personality: rights-and-options expansion (identify vulnerable standing, refuse irreversible disposal, preserve procedure, widen options, return judgment; V02 p-005 ¶347-390; V03 p-014 ¶26-31), benevolent future-scripting (V02 p-006 ¶345-424) and crisis control that universalizes a violation into a verdict on humanity while discounting his own survival (V03 p-008 ¶147-161; V12 p-008 ¶321-333). It says what selects between revision and escalation: whether a contradiction reaches a premise or relationship he still experiences as binding (the correction by Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), V02 p-006 ¶426-507; Shin (Shinei Nouzen), V08 p-002 ¶47-74; the filial interruption, V13 p-007 ¶225-249) or meets the hollow that V12 locates in the loss of his wife. It predicts his mistakes: scripting the Five into ordinary childhood, extinction rhetoric, self-exclusion from his anti-sacrifice ethic, indifference to office, and the V13 violence (p-006 ¶197-223; p-007 ¶197-222). A would overclaim: the set is one derived artifact, V04-V07 and V09-V11 have no row, the profile says V13 failed despite earlier lessons so the onset of the crisis trajectory in a new situation is not predictable from the set, and his self-worth and post-V13 partiality are OPEN. C would understate an account that says which consideration decides in each sampled class and predicts his overreach and its corrections.

The profile gives located, causally explained states of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) while stating that his modes coexist rather than progress cleanly: V02 rescue and citizenship (p-005), the self-audit about substitution (p-005 ¶474-500), future-scripting and the reenlistment shock (p-006 ¶345-424) and the revision after the 哀れみの樼 correction (p-006 ¶426-507); V03 acceptance that consensual enlistment removes any special exemption, procedural scrutiny and external safeguards (p-006; p-014); V08 anti-sacrifice planning corrected by Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (p-002); V12 self-erasure and private nihilism (p-004; p-008); V13 hostage self-disregard, violence, filial interruption and a newly partial father in the aftermath (p-006; p-007); and V14 house arrest with continuing ordinary care (p-007 ¶499-509). It forbids two regressions: 'Ernst never learns' and 'Ernst always learns immediately'. C would understate located transitions with causes and controls. A is rejected: V04-V07 and V09-V11 have no row, V14 is one ordinary scene, the profile's shift from knowing the healthy future to preserving later choices is only MODERATE-to-HIGH and not globally complete, and nothing after V14 is established.

The profile fixes the written-Japanese register of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman): 僕 as the stable first person through household joking, politics, command and private despair, with 私 only in a marked public context; casual だよ, だろう, ね and かな carrying absolute propositions in a conversational shell (人類なんて滅んでしまえばいいんだよ); an instantaneous switch into the voice of a head of state, narrated in V03 after 僕一応連邦軍の最高指揮官だからね？ (p-007 ¶66-138); father-language that is joking and aspirational in V02 (お父さんって呼んでくれてもいいんだよ？) and charged by V13 (おとうさん, p-007 ¶225-249); moral anger that becomes colder rather than louder (酷薄, thin smile, low sigh); paternal panic (どうしてさ!?, V02 p-006 reenlistment rows); and private despair stripped of rhetoric (そうだよ, どうでもいいんだよ, 彼女はもう──いないんだから, V12 p-008 ¶321-333), with 帰ってきなさい as a repeated command. C would understate a located idiolect, state deltas and exemplars. A is rejected: there is no frequency data, the forms he uses to address Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) and the other children are not given, no located exemplar of the marked public 私 is given, and the L09 voice ledger is outside the set.

The profile treats ordinary life as indispensable for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) and states its drivers: informality and play as his real social mode, future capability for the children, and workaholic absence that leaves continuous household labor to Teresa, the household partner. Located conduct includes reports on civilian adaptation read under other documents (V02 p-006 ¶65-90), household boundaries and curiosity (V02 p-005 ¶443-461), small observational fathering (Alter.1 part0022), the bus and snow-walk panic about transport (part0025), the welcome party for Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and Annette (Annette Penrose) (part0050), lecturing injured Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) and sulking after cards (part0051), the house as a social node (part0052), being hunted down by Teresa in a game (part0062) and childhood memory, food and care under house arrest (V14 p-007 ¶499-509). C would understate stated drivers with paragraph-located conduct. A is rejected: there is no routine or frequency, Alter.1 rows are not placed by volume, and several items (television and coffee rules, curfews, school research) have no row of their own.

Directed relations of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) are analyzed with distinct registers: Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), guardianship, concealment, household scolding and an anti-sacrifice boundary, ending with おとうさん as a binding claim (V02 p-005 ¶443-461; V08 p-002; V13 p-007 ¶225-249); Shin (Shinei Nouzen), protected by reducing his own side's discretion (V03 p-014 ¶26-31) and able to contradict him (V08 p-002), with the miscalibrated 反抗期 joke (V13 p-007 ¶197-222); the Five collectively, modeled longitudinally from rescue through civilianization and revision to soldiers without special exemption (V02; V03); Theo (Theoto Rikka), who sees his ugly side without the filial history (V13 p-007); Teresa, household partner and truth-teller who refuses the substitution premise and is not a replacement romance (V02 p-005 ¶474-500; V13 p-007 ¶770-784); Grethe (Grethe Wenzel), a pre-office childhood friendship (V14 p-007); military command and officials (V03; V12 p-004); and the electorate. C would understate this partner-specific discrimination. A is rejected: Raiden (Raiden Shuga) appears only in the reenlistment rows and Kurena (Kurena Kukumila) and Anju (Anju Emma) are not separated from the Five, Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and Annette (Annette Penrose) are sampled only in Alter.1, reverse directions are rarely analyzed, and the relationship matrix and L02 are outside the set.

Private states of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) are located mainly through his own rare disclosures and embodied cues: asking Teresa, the household partner, whether taking the children in is a 愚かしい代償行為 (V02 p-005 ¶474-500); the private admission that nothing matters because his wife is gone (V12 p-008 ¶321-333); and the V13 sequence in which the weapon slips, he covers his face and cries at おとうさん (p-007 ¶225-249). These states drive located conduct and explain the danger in his extinction rhetoric. B would overclaim: the profile says his self-disclosures are relatively rare, it classifies no exemplar as focalized narration or inner speech, his interior across V03-V08 is inferred from conduct and others' perception (Theo (Theoto Rikka) recognizing the void, V13 p-007 ¶197-222), and whether he develops independent self-worth is OPEN. D would understate located disclosures that carry the profile's explanation.

The profile states the conflict style of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman): at his best he separates motive, right, method and consequence, saying that exclusion can arise from love and fear but cannot bypass speech, agreed rules and accountability through secret violence (V03 p-006 ¶59-92); at his worst he jumps from condemning a wrong to foreclosing every answer to it. He argues downward, sideways and upward because status does not settle truth for him, struggles most with contradiction that attacks his identity as protector, interprets before listening (V02 p-006 ¶360-424), revises when the hidden premise is struck and then narrows rather than abandons the value (p-006 ¶426-507; V08 p-002), and in crisis escalates into cold calm and violence (V13 p-006 ¶197-223; p-007 ¶197-222). Repair is behavioral before rhetorical. C would understate conditioned response families with located corrections. A is rejected: V13 is an exceptional state that does not transfer as policy, conflicts in V04-V07 and V09-V11 are unsampled, and what triggers the crisis branch in a new situation is not established.

The profile gives Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) argued positions with a failure mode: nonexpendability against reducing a person to security risk, research material or imperial resource (V02 p-005 ¶347-378; V03 p-014; V08 p-002); procedural correction, so that fear cannot secretly override an agreed rule (the 消毒 question, V03 p-006 ¶59-92); no special exemption for his children once enlistment is consensual (V03); return as part of duty (V03 p-007); and the V13 claim that love can create exclusion and cannot excuse refusal to improve (p-006 ¶197-223). Its counterexample audit narrows them: he resists sacrificing others more consistently than himself, the polity or humanity, and personal corrigibility is no constitutional guarantee. It predicts the error of universalizing a violation into extinction rhetoric and of treating his own office as irrelevant (V12 p-004 ¶587-602). C would understate located positions with a reasoning pattern and stated asymmetry. A is rejected: post-V13 partiality toward his children and his self-worth are OPEN, and the constitutional questions are routed to OQ1-OQ4 outside the set.

The profile gives the comic forms of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman): status deflation (僕一応連邦軍の最高指揮官だからね？, V03 p-007), embarrassing parent energy (V02 p-005 ¶381-390), eccentric overreaction (the bus scene ending in a fantasy of punching the Republic's president, Alter.1 part0025), losing status safely (cards and the game, part0051, part0062), and teasing an old friend (Grethe (Grethe Wenzel), V14 p-007). It states that humor failing under crisis is a marker of impairment, not relief (V13 p-007 ¶197-222), and that he can be mocked or ignored at home without an authority crisis. C would understate functional forms with paragraph-located controls and a crisis condition. A is rejected: several forms rest on Alter.1 without volume placement, household humor dominates, and no stop rule for embarrassing enthusiasm is given.

A dedicated canonical profile of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) over V02-V14 with Alter.1 supplemental, with 232 diagnostic rows, every one routed to volume, XHTML file and paragraph: V02 88, V03 27, V08 12, V12 19, V13 52, V14 8 and Alter.1 26. B would overclaim: V04-V07 and V09-V11 have no row, so seven of the thirteen volumes in his range are unsampled; rows carry one shared gloss per scene group rather than their own event description; the bank does not mark which rows carry a Phase-5 locator; and the narrower authorities that govern conflicts (L01, L02, L03, L08, L09, Documents 06 and 09, and the matrix) are outside the set. D would understate a dense, paragraph-routed bank whose groups reach every state the profile names.

For Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) there is a five-claim counterexample audit with dispositions (care survives but narrowed, autonomy narrowed, anti-sacrifice survives with a major asymmetry, corrigibility rejected as a guarantee, fatherhood narrowed), thirty-two mischaracterization traps and forty would-sound-wrong constraints. Located negatives include Teresa, the household partner, refusing the substitution premise (V02 p-005 ¶474-500), the V03 refusal of special exemption, V12 private nihilism against reading his absolutism as heroic conviction (p-008 ¶321-333), the V13 violence against 'too gentle for violence' (p-006 ¶197-223) and the head of state as a wheezing comic target without status crisis (Alter.1 part0062). C would understate these affirmative, located constraints. A is rejected: many constraints are profile rules without a row, and limits after V14 are open.

Every scene-bank row for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) is located by volume, XHTML file and paragraph, and three volumes are split inside themselves: V02 between rescue (p-005 ¶283-414), self-audit (¶474-500), future-scripting and reenlistment conflict (p-006 ¶345-424) and correction (¶426-507); V03 between procedural scrutiny (p-006), command (p-007), absolutist rhetoric (p-008) and safeguards (p-014); and V13 between hostage (p-006 ¶24-40), moral conflict (¶197-223), violence (p-007 ¶197-222), interruption (¶225-249) and aftermath (¶770-784). B would overclaim: V04-V07 and V09-V11 have no row and no state at all, V14 is one ordinary scene, the profile names no developmental protocol or default state, and Alter.1 rows are unplaced. D would understate paragraph routes and the in-volume splits at V02, V03 and V13.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with 僕 and casual だよ, だろう, ね and かな as the baseline in household, political and private speech; 私 only in a marked public context.

Command speech is terse and role-dense after a visible switch; dangerous moral anger is cold and quiet rather than shouted; private despair is plain and short; father-language is joking before V13 and charged after it.
Forms of address toward individual children, officials and strangers are not invented beyond what the profile gives.
No frequency distribution, anime performance or state after V14 is claimed, and output that depends on one abstains.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains first person, particles, state switching and exemplars enough for illustrative output with sampled relations. Unattested address forms and missing frequency data restrict form rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected state; there is no default. The states are: V02 before or after the correction by Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) (p-006 ¶426-507); V03 after consensual enlistment (p-006 to p-014); V08 after the correction by Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (p-002); V12 self-erasure (p-004; p-008); V13 before the violence (p-006 ¶24-223) or after the filial interruption (p-007 ¶225-784); or the V14 house-arrest boundary (p-007 ¶499-509). V04-V07 and V09-V11 are not used, nothing after V14 is used, and Alter.1 rows do not fix a state.

The V13 violence (p-007 ¶197-222) is an exceptional crisis state, not a transferable policy; a scenario may model his susceptibility to crisis escalation but does not reproduce that state outside its conditions.

The interlocutor is a profiled relation in its attested register: Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), Shin (Shinei Nouzen), the Five collectively, Theo (Theoto Rikka), Teresa, the household partner, Grethe (Grethe Wenzel), or military command and officials. Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Kurena (Kurena Kukumila) and Anju (Anju Emma) individually, and Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and Annette (Annette Penrose) outside the Alter.1 household, are a separate, lower-confidence transfer, as is an unfamiliar person.

The situation matches a sampled class: an unknown or vulnerable person whose disposal is proposed, a child choosing a danger he fears, emergency necessity used to launder prejudice, a strategic resource that could be spent, his own office or survival at stake, a contradiction aimed at his hidden premise, or ordinary household, transport and celebration life.

Output predicts his characteristic errors (future-scripting, extinction rhetoric, self-exclusion, indifference to his office, joking paternal language that misfits a crisis) and abstains on his political future after V14, the postwar household and whether fatherhood has given him independent self-worth.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected state at the located turns: V02 p-006 ¶426-507; V03 p-006 to p-014; V08 p-002; V12 p-004 and p-008; V13 before p-006 ¶197-223 or after p-007 ¶225-249; the V14 boundary at p-007 ¶499-509. No default, no V04-V07 or V09-V11 state, no state after V14, no transferable use of the V13 violence, and no chronological use of Alter.1.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), Shin (Shinei Nouzen), the Five collectively, Theo (Theoto Rikka), Teresa, the household partner, Grethe (Grethe Wenzel), or military command and officials, in their attested registers. Individual members of the Five other than Shin and Theo, Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and Annette (Annette Penrose) outside the Alter.1 household, and unfamiliar people are a separate, lower-confidence transfer.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to sampled relations, situation classes and one explicitly selected state at located turns. Unsampled volumes, the V13 violence as a policy and his political future are excluded rather than inferred.

conditions: Sampled ordinary classes only: reading reports buried in work, household rules and scolding, transport worries, welcome parties, card games and group games, holidays, food and childhood memory.
He is often absent for state work and Teresa, the household partner, carries daily continuity; he can be ignored, mocked or beaten without any authority crisis.
No invented daily routine, hobbies or household arrangements beyond what the profile attests.
scenario_readiness.note: Recurring located ordinary conduct with stated drivers supports bounded extrapolation. The absence of routine and frequency blocks READY.

conditions: Situation classes the profile samples: disposal or exploitation of vulnerable people, fear or prejudice laundered through emergency necessity, consent and its limits, exemption from lawful risk, sacrifice of a strategic person, and his own office or survival.
Reasoning separates motive, right, method and consequence at its best and can jump to totalizing verdicts at its worst; he applies anti-sacrifice to others more consistently than to himself.
The selected state matters: before the V02 correction he scripts the Five's future; after V13 family love restrains him but may also weight his judgment toward his children.
No decision on constitutional survival, emergency powers or his return to office.
scenario_readiness.note: Located positions with a stated asymmetry and failure mode support bounded ethical extrapolation within the sampled classes.

The profile gives no romance for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) within the boundary: his wife and unborn child appear only through bereavement (V02 p-005 ¶474-500; V12 p-008 ¶321-333), treating Teresa, the household partner, as a replacement romance or substitute wife is a listed trap and constraint that the profile says the source resists, and the profile leaves no open romantic thread to model. CONDITIONAL would require inventing a relationship state the evidence affirmatively declines.

conditions: His role is provisional President and supreme commander: quarantine and inspection without military exploitation (V02 p-005 ¶347-378), citizenship (¶381-390), procedural scrutiny (V03 p-006), the command switch and operation orders (V03 p-007), external oversight around Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (V03 p-014), protection planning for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) (V08 p-002), refugee-volunteer policy (V12 p-004) and succession competence as a hostage (V13 p-006 ¶24-40).

He accepts lawful limits on his authority and asks whether prejudice is laundered through necessity, but may treat electoral backing as authorization to embody the ideal and his own office as irrelevant.
No restored office, legal sanction or postwar political role is modeled after V13 removes his effective authority.
scenario_readiness.note: Sampled executive, command and institutional reasoning, including its stated failure modes, supports bounded extrapolation within one selected state.

known_limits.statement: The source boundary is locked original-Japanese V02-V14 for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), with Alter.1 supplemental and Alter.2 excluded. V13 leaves him formally president without effective authority and V14 under house arrest; his political future, the postwar household, his self-worth and whether family partiality can endanger the polity are OPEN, and constitutional questions are routed to OQ1-OQ4.

The V13 violence of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) (p-006 ¶197-223; p-007 ¶197-222) is a crisis expression of a real latent structure, not his baseline, and the profile says it occurred despite earlier corrections, so the set does not establish what would trigger the crisis trajectory in a new situation.
The filial claim おとうさん binds Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) from V13 (p-007 ¶225-249) but does not retroactively validate earlier guardianship or establish how every member of the Five conceives of him.

The profile of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) is a derived reconstruction reference whose header subordinates it to the Japanese source and the narrower canonical V2 authorities (L01, L02, L09 and the thematic Documents), none of which is curated on this row; for exact wording it routes through the shared CMR locator index, which is not curated here.
The scene bank has no row for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) in V04-V07 or V09-V11, and V14 has a single ordinary scene, so states in those volumes cannot be selected.

The profile does not classify any exemplar for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) as narration, inner speech or dialogue, and outside two private disclosures and the V13 interruption his interior is inferred from conduct.
The profile makes no claim about pitch, prosody or performed voice for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman); voice claims cover written Japanese only.
